title: Longest Happy Prefix
description: A string is called a happy prefix if it is a non-empty proper prefix of `s` that is also a suffix of `s` (excluding `s` itself). Given a lowercase string `s`, return its longest happy prefix, or an empty string `""` if no happy prefix exists.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.
hints: The KMP prefix function (LPS array) computes, for every prefix, the length of its longest proper border.
The answer is simply the first lps[n - 1] characters of s.

examples.explanation: The prefix "l" of length 1 is also a suffix of "level".
The prefix "abab" of length 4 is also a suffix of "ababab".
No non-empty proper prefix of "leetcode" is also a suffix.
